description: Localized, dependency-driven compiler for permanent L4 product contracts and deterministic L5 delivery contracts.
principles: The root LLM detects the communication language, translates friendly step titles and creates the visible roadmap before clarification begins.

The runtime prefixes exactly the six E1-through-E6 human checkpoints with the deterministic 👤 marker; E7-through-E10 and dynamically appended technical nodes remain automated, and persisted localized titles remain plain reusable text.
E4 parallel children are dispatched by stable entity: selectors and reconstruct their base invocation when collab-messages omits planning or prompt metadata on materialized fan-out children.

Every E4, E7 and E8 parallel artifact worker submits a strict-tool flexible envelope. The envelope is a valid collab-messages payload, so healthy workers never transiently enter the failed state before their deterministic after-prompt gate runs.
E4, E7 and E8 readers accept the platform tool-call transport (`flexible.result.arguments`) as well as direct flexible and legacy raw artifacts before applying their deterministic gate.
Nested artifact schemas used by a worker tool hoist $defs to the function-parameters root and omit the embedded $id; strict providers resolve root-relative refs from that root.
Dynamic E4 dispatch is symmetric: before-prompt prefers hook args, while after-prompt falls back to the selector retained in step.prompt when collab-messages omits callback args.
E2 normalizes every journey step entity to one stable PascalCase identifier; E4 consumes that exact id for its entity or projection instead of comparing a localized display label.

The journey context graph is derived, never declared. E2 owns narrative, step sequence, step kind and step entity; helpers/ns4Context.ts is the single place that derives every context from (entity, cardinality, origin) for E7, E8 and E9. requiresContext, providesContext and entry.carries do not exist in any artifact.

A derived contextId is a pure function of its entity, so contexts are keyed by entity across the catalog, the E9 store and every route: one cardinality comes from the step kind (locate resolves many into one; inspect, act, decide and handoff operate on one).

Coordination comes from the approved ontology plus the journey sequence, not from a declared name: an act or decide step additionally requires every required manyToOne parent of its entity, and a step requires its own entity only when an earlier step of the same journey already provides it, which is what separates maintenance from creation.

A context origin is structural and resolved in this order: hub anchor through routeOf, picker slice of the same entity located earlier in the journey, actor session through the E3 profile data scope, and the sending step entity of a handoff. An event-driven journey with no internal sender carries the entity of its first step.

Findings are classified before task status changes: broken contracts, references, envelopes or infrastructure are terminal Type A failures; business bifurcations are Type B system decisions; deterministic repairs are Type C resolutions. Type B and resolvable Type C findings are recorded and never fail the task.

All semantic gates use helpers/ns4Resolve.ts. It applies the generator's implicit Type B choice or an explicit Type C patch, returns the resolved artifact plus durable systemDecisions, and leaves Type A or mechanically unresolved findings for terminal handling.
E2 proposals pass a deterministic structural gate before an independent 🔎 semantic coverage judge; the structural repair budget is separate from the single semantic complete-draft repair budget.

E2 policy decisions are explicit journey contracts: generation declares chosen alternatives without impact, the independent judge adds impact and related journeys, and human selections are preserved in the approved journey index.

A human policy selection different from the generated choice always starts a complete next-round E2 rewrite. A deterministic honor gate rejects a rewritten draft that does not make each selected choice its chosen value.

E2 linear steps cannot combine creation and maintenance when their context preconditions differ; the judge requires separate outcome journeys and repair instructions are placed after the complete draft.

E2 semantic coverage receives at most one focused patch repair. Remaining coverage bifurcations become recorded system decisions using the behavior already implicit in the generated draft, and the human review opens without failing the task.

After the E2 structural gate passes, code computes the complete module step-kind histogram. The evidence-backed moduleWithoutDecide signal is sent to the existing coverage judge, may consume the same single semantic repair, and never becomes a blocking gate; a surviving signal becomes a visible journey policy decision.
E1 preserves its full reviewed contract, supports repeated prompt-driven revisions and only unlocks compilation after the rich deterministic gate passes.
E2 through E6 approval callbacks persist their already-gated permanent review artifacts before adding the result anchor; E7 is an automated compiler after the sixth checkpoint.
Every implemented compile step writes a permanent L4 artifact and a stable result anchor.

Every permanent TypeScript artifact imports its canonical artifact interface from agentNewSolution4/types.ts, is emitted with as const satisfies and exports its exact typeof contract; module, journey, access, ontology and rule shape drift therefore fails tsc while module-specific literal unions remain available without copied strings.
Permanent L4 artifacts plus their approved module checkpoint are the resume authority; pipeline state is monotonic and is reconciled from those artifacts if a late callback lags behind.

A single module-name invocation is canonicalized before the root planner: BuildFlowFsm23 resolves to the existing buildFlowFsm23 folder, so resume never creates a fresh E1 tree before checking pipeline ownership.
A completed result anchor carries the bounded approved contract needed by the immediately unlocked successor, avoiding a storage-index visibility race between client hooks.
Module and index artifacts retain userLanguage and localized stepTitles for maintenance and resume context; per-item E7 artifacts do not repeat it.
Terminal step failures use traceMsg in the task and persist status, error and failedAt in the pipeline whenever a module pipeline already exists.
The pipeline folder is working state for one run and is never a source of truth: every contract a later step reads is a permanent L4 artifact, so discarding pipeline/ loses nothing but the trace.
Previous flow versions are never migrated automatically.
The /fast flag uses the same deterministic gates and persistence paths; E1 auto-accepts its clarification and valid E2-E6 proposals are approved without opening their widgets.

E1 records modernization strategies now; E4 currently compiles only explicit new-solution ontology contracts and fails closed for modernization instead of fabricating a greenfield or replacement database.
E4 classifies every entity into an explicit persistence target: shared MDM for stable base records, module database for transactions, or derived/external/embedded storage for non-table concepts.

Every E4 lifecycle declares its initial state and optional terminal states explicitly; E7 copies that contract mechanically rather than inferring lifecycle meaning from state ordering or missing outgoing transitions.

E4 first freezes a compact ontology overview, then details entities through the proven parallel_dynamic fan-out with maxParallel 20, binds every relationship to exact existing endpoint fields or an explicit non-FK realization, and only then opens one human review.
E2, E3 and E4 carry business-rule references only as stable useRules ids; descriptions exist exactly once in rules/rules.defs.ts.

E5 reconstructs its inputs from approved permanent journey, access and ontology artifacts, collects useRules mechanically and creates one concise rule catalog instead of compiling executable rule objects.

E3, E4 and E5 use one shared approved-artifact reader: journey and ontology indexes plus their per-item defs, and the access-matrix def. Recovery never depends on the large E2/E4 pipeline drafts; E4 entity repair reads only the matching prior entity def.
E5 uses one reasoning call, one deterministic gate and at most one bounded repair. The gate requires every useRules id referenced by E2-E4 to have one description.

E6 is the sixth and final clarification: one conservative reasoning call reviews only justified horizontal modules and external plugins, accepts an empty recommendation list and excludes platform baseline capabilities.
The historical e6-behaviors runtime plan id remains a stable internal identifier; the permanent artifact uses composition terminology and previous flow versions are rejected rather than migrated.
Future pages, use cases, tables and maintenance operations scan the complete L4 and attach only useRules ids; changing a rule description never requires copying text into its consumers.
E7 mechanically groups identical journey step ids into stable N-to-one channel-neutral use cases, details them with a maxParallel 20 fan-out and runs one targeted repair round for invalid drafts.
E7 preserves every journey businessHash and compiles small reusable behaviors with derived context ids, ontology entity refs, behavior-owned rule ids and references to valid lifecycle transitions.

E7 compiles only lifecycle states reachable through approved journey transitions. Build and gate share one reachability definition; shrink iterates to a fixed point, removes transitions whose sources disappear, records every removed state and newly dormant predicate as a system decision with an operateState alternative, omits workflows with no remaining transition, and never mutates the approved E4 ontology.
Use cases do not copy E3 actors, authorities or scopes and do not prescribe ports, repositories, storage routing or backend architecture. E3 owns authorization and E8 owns channel integration.

E8 derives workspace partition, page context, slices, invalidations, hub candidacy and navigation candidates from approved L4 contracts; its LLM calls may only localize presentation and select a closed surface catalog.

E8 hosts an act or decide scenario of a satellite entity in the workspace of the anchor it points at through a required manyToOne relationship, so a scenario is never isolated in a workspace without slices. E8 keeps pageContext only for the hub anchor and contexts carried by a real notification or handoff edge. Other required contexts remain scenario-local selections resolved by a slice, form input or actor session; no context carries URL classification metadata.

A screen is a journey, a record catalogue or an anchor hub — E8 never invents a fourth kind and never partitions steps into workspaces. Tier 1 is one CRUD workspace per persisted business entity, tier 2 is one workspace per approved journey, tier 3 is the hub of the dominant anchor plus standalone projections.
E8 is the single owner of every workspace. E9 takes no screen decision at all: it transposes the approved E8 model into the classic L4 format and nothing else.

A journey workspace emits one query bffCall per locate/inspect step and one command bffCall per act/decide step; each section points its organisms at those ids. One bffCall carries at most one collection, so composition is expressed as several calls on one page, never as slices inside one envelope.

The origin a page renders by is the operation input source, in the client-boundary vocabulary: userInput renders a form field, selectedEntity renders a picker, routeParam comes from the URL, and every other source is resolved at runtime and never rendered.
A literal union reaches the page through the ontology, never through a source label: an enumerated field carries its values on the field and a lifecycle carries them on the entity.

Exactly two LLM calls remain in E8: the hub dashboard composition over a closed catalogue and the presentation labels. Neither may add, remove or rename a structural id; an invalid answer after one repair falls back to the deterministic default and records a system decision.

E8 freezes its mechanically derived and strictly gated skeleton automatically. Its workspace-detail fan-out is bounded to 20 workers, validates each worker independently, and writes permanent typed workspace artifacts plus a workspace index without opening a clarification.

Every constrained E8 presentation-repair step created by the runtime has one exact dynamic plan-id contract and is routed symmetrically through the E8 before/after hooks; malformed lookalike ids remain unsupported.

An E8 selection input with an invalid sourceRef is repaired without another LLM call only when its fieldRef identifies exactly one compatible frozen slice; zero or multiple candidates remain Type A failures.
E8 awaits its deterministic finalizer inside the local failure boundary so an irrecoverable detail persists failed pipeline state instead of leaving E8 marked running.
E8 dispatch is idempotent by the stable workspace-detail planId; a repeated or late after-prompt callback cannot enqueue a second fan-out or finalizer for the same compilation round.

E9 is a zero-LLM deterministic compiler. It reads only approved E2-E8 permanent artifacts, validates navigation reachability and context provenance, and emits typed BFF contracts, route/store/notification contracts plus realized operation authorities without a checkpoint.

E8 previews and E9 compiles routes through the same total helpers/routeOf.ts projection. Routes derive only from module, hub/place structure and a unique primary scenario target; zero or multiple targets omit the item id and record a system decision instead of failing.
E9 validates notification deep links by carried contextId against routeOf output, never by idFieldRef text; a local selection may legitimately share an id field name with a route identity.

Every E9 finding is Type A and records whether it came from the approved E8 skeleton or from E9 emission. Skeleton failures mark E8 stale and return repair ownership to E8; compiler failures preserve E8 approval and replay only E9. E9 never emits a partial approval anchor.

E9 BFF inputs are a discriminated data-or-decision contract. Data inputs retain strict ontology fieldRef validation, including editable userDecision fields already carrying a fieldRef. A verb decision is the E8 userDecision form with a policy sourceRef and no fieldRef; it carries approved E7 transitionIds as a literal-union catalog and deterministic label, or unknown plus a non-blocking warning when the use case has no transitions.
E9 emissions are canonical and timestamp-free. Identical approved E8/E7/E4/E3 inputs produce byte-identical typed defs on every run.

E10 first validates the complete saved L4 graph and emits no L5 delivery when a blocking check fails. Resolution, journey reachability, decision coherence, compiled workflow health and source-hash staleness are deterministic errors with an explicit owning repair step.

E10 disclosure and dormant-command checks are registrars. Disclosure never compares E3 prose with field ids; dormant commands remain visible and produce an auditable system decision naming their missing compiled transition evidence.

E10 writes an additive l5/config.json module-navigation seed, frontend/backend owner queues and a stable process record only after validate-all passes. Existing unrelated config keys, projects and modules are preserved.
After validate-all and L5 delivery succeed, E10 deterministically records automatic approval, adds e10-result and marks the module artifact and pipeline complete without opening a clarification.

invocation.resumeRule: A v35-owned incomplete module starts a localized root plan and resumes at the first incomplete implemented step. Module-name lookup accepts an initial-capital or other canonical-equivalent spelling and retains the actual normalized folder name. Previous flow versions are not migrated; foreign or older modules are rejected.

orchestration.treeCreation: after root LLM, before any human clarification
orchestration.roadmapExecution: E1 through E10 are implemented. E1 through E6 are the six human checkpoints; E7 through E10 run automatically, and a successful E10 compile completes the pipeline.

steps.goal: Confirm the complete initial product contract: identity, review policy, solution/modernization strategy, business scope, localization and declared constraints.
runtimeNotes: The root plan seeds the localized clarification and the full normalized review is preserved in its answer anchor.
A human change request adds the next open E1 round before completing the current clarification.
Validation failures remain visible inside the same widget and do not mark the step or pipeline failed.
/fast uses the same widget event with autoAcceptSeconds=10.
LLM failures return through afterPrompt and remain visible in the task trace.

steps.goal: Validate and write the initial permanent module contract.
Generate, adjust and approve permanent connected business journeys.
runtimeNotes: prompt_ready preserves the hook args byte-for-byte.
E2 is marked running only after the LLM call returns to afterPrompt.
Terminal failures are persisted in pipeline.steps.e2.error and failedAt.
A deterministic gate failure persists the invalid draft and may schedule one bounded structural repair for the current proposal cycle.
A structurally valid draft is not shown immediately: an independent reasoning-model judge compares all E1 actors, capabilities, screen intents and outcomes with E2.
The generated candidate uses an internal flexible payload so it cannot flash as a human clarification before gate and judge approval.
The coverage judge rejects missing recipient journeys, orphan user outcomes, raw-id risks and human-selectable references without named context acquisition or a credible lookup source.

The runtime sends the original sourcePrompt plus a mechanical whole-module step-kind histogram to the judge. Only moduleWithoutDecide is active: decide=0 requires one business-language coverage issue; decide>=1 suppresses that signal.

One complete-draft semantic repair is allowed independently of structural repair. After that single attempt, remaining semantic coverage findings become system decisions whose defaultChoice is the behavior already implicit in the generated draft.

A surviving moduleWithoutDecide issue is recorded on the judge-selected existing journey as a policyDecision whose chosen value preserves the current no-decision behavior and whose alternatives remain selectable in the existing checkpoint. It is excluded from systemDecision conversion.

If the judge is unavailable, omits an active moduleWithoutDecide signal or returns another invalid response, one retry remains allowed; exhaustion records a localized systemDecision that decision coverage was not evaluated and continues to the normal checkpoint instead of failing the task.
An invalid judge envelope is retried once. Compact judge results remain in the task trace after large LLM interactions are cleaned.

Every structurally valid draft opens the 👤 widget after the judge round unless /fast is active. Judged-complete is not a prerequisite; assumed decisions are shown read-only in a collapsed Decisões assumidas section. In /fast, the same generated choices and system decisions are persisted automatically after gate and judge without creating the clarification widget.
Generation declares journey policy decisions before journeys and never supplies impact; the independent judge is the only stage that may add decision impact and related journeys.

Selecting an alternative or requesting free-text changes preserves the current versioned draft, starts a full replacement round, and passes the deterministic selected-choice honor gate before the widget can reopen.

Approval persists every decision selection, including unchanged generated choices, in the journey index. A deterministic E2 impact report records the full step-kind histogram and downstream E3-E7 contracts made stale by changed, added or removed journeys.

A step declares stepId, kind, entity, title, description and featureRefs. It never declares a context: requiresContext, providesContext and entry.carries do not exist and cannot be reintroduced as optional hints.

entry declares only its mode and an optional preferredFromJourneyRef; the entry context of an event-driven journey is derived from the sending handoff step, or from its own first step when no internal sender exists.
A handoff step names the receiving E3 profile in targetProfile, which is the only routing fact E9 needs to compile its notification.
The E2 structural gate checks step identity, kind, entity shape, sequence and feature references. Context provenance is not an E2 concern because there is no declared context left to check.
Journey rule references are stored only in business.useRules as lower-camel ids; E2 never copies rule descriptions.

steps.goal: Generate, iteratively adjust and approve the collab-auth access matrix, data scopes and disclosure boundaries.
runtimeNotes: Each human change request adds the next open E3 round before completing the current clarification.
Every round returns to the same localized matrix widget until explicit approval.
Authorities follow the lowercase collab-auth domain:code convention and remain opaque to the agent.
External grants cannot use organization-wide scope.
Limited disclosure records an enforceable projection intent; hiding fields in the frontend is insufficient.
The /fast path validates and approves the same E3 contract without opening the widget.
The e3-result handoff carries the approved review, approval metadata and permanent artifact path for the immediately unlocked E4 hook.
Late or duplicate callbacks cannot regress an approved E3 pipeline state to running, waitingHuman or failed.
Terminal failures are persisted in pipeline.steps.e3.error and failedAt.
Grant rule references are stored only in grants[].useRules; descriptions remain owned by E5.

steps.goal: Generate, directly annotate, structurally adjust and approve the connected greenfield business ontology.
runtimeNotes: The first reasoning call returns only the frozen cross-entity overview: entity identity, source refs, lifecycle states and predicates, MDM/storage routing and relationships; it does not generate fields or rule descriptions.
Before entity fan-out, the overview gate requires every required E2 carried or produced businessObject to exist as an E4 entity or projection with the same id.
One parallel_dynamic child then details each entity with filtered E2/E3 context; maxParallel is 20, matching the proven agentNewSolution ontology implementation.

Parallel children complete with trace on provider or gate failure so one entity cannot fail the fan-out; the deterministic finalizer runs one targeted parallel repair round for only missing or invalid entities.
The finalizer reassembles the unchanged human E4 review contract and reruns the complete journey/access/relationship gate before opening one widget or approving /fast.
The run carries solutionMode=new explicitly; it never infers or fabricates a legacy database contract.
E4 consumes the permanent access/access-matrix.defs.ts artifact; during the immediate E3-to-E4 transition it may consume the identical approved contract carried by e3-result.

Stable base registrations such as clients, projects, regions and material catalogs are proposed as organization-scoped MDM; orders, movements, logs, invoices and other transactions use the module database.
Master data and operational state are separate entities: a Material catalog may be MDM while inventory balance, adjustment and usage remain transactional.
Every entity carries a structured storage target, scope, identifier and MDM type when applicable; the ontology index repeats this compact persistence routing for L1/L2 compilers.

Static field constraints are shared validation contracts: backend enforcement is mandatory and frontend mirrors them for early feedback. Named lifecycle meanings required by sources are frozen as exact lifecycle predicate-to-state mappings; dynamic, time-relative, cross-entity and authorization conditions remain E5 rules.
Every non-empty lifecycle declares one initialState and may declare terminalStates; the E4 gate verifies membership and rejects an initial state marked terminal.
The review widget groups entities by persistence destination and highlights cross-store relationships before approval.
The review widget separates safe direct title/description edits from structural LLM requests.
Before a structural revision, the current draft including direct human edits is persisted and supplied to the next round.
A first deterministic gate failure persists the draft and schedules one bounded LLM repair step before failing the task.
Every E2 journey, now feature and E3 information authority remains traceable from the ontology.
After entity fan-out, one compact reasoning pass binds every semantic relationship to exact existing endpoint fields, or explicitly declares an MDM/derived realization without a fake foreign key.
The binding gate rejects missing relationships, invented fields, endpoint drift and persistence-strategy mismatches; one localized binding repair is allowed before failure.
Relationships must preserve selected business context so later screens never require typed foreign-key ids.
Approval writes one permanent defs file per entity plus a small ontology index with the frozen hash.
Each human change request adds the next open E4 round before completing the current clarification.
Terminal failures persist the invalid draft when available and pipeline.steps.e4.error/failedAt.
Entity rule references are stored only in useRules; static field constraints remain typed data validation contracts rather than catalog business rules.

steps.goal: Create one human-readable source of truth for every business-rule id referenced by L4.
runtimeNotes: prompt_ready preserves the original hook args byte-for-byte so proposal and repair stages cannot lose their round identity.
The runtime mechanically collects the unique useRules ids present in approved journeys, access grants and ontology entities.
One reasoning call receives those ids and compact approved L4 context, then returns only id and one precise human-readable description per rule.
The deterministic gate rejects duplicate or invalid ids and any referenced id without a description; unrelated catalog rules are allowed for future consumers.
One transport retry and one deterministic-gate repair are bounded; E5 has no per-rule fan-out, executable policy schema or independent judge.
Static scalar field constraints remain in E4 and are not duplicated as business rules.
A human change request persists the edited draft and adds the next open E5 round before completing the current clarification.
Approval writes one rules/rules.defs.ts catalog and an approved review snapshot for future maintenance and L1/L2 compilation.
Later page, use-case, table and behavior compilers scan the complete L4 for matching rule ids and store only useRules references.

steps.goal: Conservatively review whether realization needs an additional horizontal business module or external plugin.
runtimeNotes: This is the sixth and final human clarification before realization.
One compact reasoning call consumes approved E1, journeys, ontology and rules; fields and access details are omitted from the prompt.
An empty recommendation list is valid and preferred when approved L4 has no evidence for an addition.
Authentication/RBAC, i18n, tenant isolation, files, LLM proxy, messages/tasks, monitoring and auditing are platform baseline and cannot become recommendations.
Recommendations contain only id, kind, title, purpose and include/defer decision; implementation design is deferred to E7.
One transport retry and one deterministic-gate repair are bounded; there is no fan-out or independent judge.
A human may approve immediately or request another conservative proposal through the same localized 6/6 widget.
The stable e6-behaviors runtime id is internal; only modules owned by the current flow version may resume.

steps.goal: Compile approved journeys into small channel- and architecture-neutral business behaviors and lifecycle workflows.
runtimeNotes: The plan is mechanical: identical stable step ids converge into one use case and every journey step remains covered through compiledFrom.
One parallel_dynamic reasoning child describes each behavior from filtered journey, ontology and rule context; maxParallel is 20.
Context requires/provides are exact E2 ids; context lineage remains compiled mechanically in journey realization instead of being copied into use cases.
E5 rules are candidates and the use case references only rules enforced by its own behavior.
Draft contract versions are explicit. A resume reuses only drafts from the current simple contract and never migrates the previous oversized shape silently.
The gate validates descriptions, exact E2 contexts, E4 entity refs, existing E5 ids and valid lifecycle transitions; field selection and persistence are not part of the use-case contract.

Actors, authorities and scopes remain in E3; inputs, outputs, errors, pagination, selection, projections and route binding remain in E8 or downstream generation; ports, transactions and adapters are implementation choices.

A deterministic finalizer records every gate issue in e7-validation-report.json, repairs only invalid or missing use cases once, derives workflows, writes typed permanent artifacts and advances to E8.

The E7 validation report reader and writer share one schema-version constant. Every finalizer merges its round by round number, preserving earlier findings and replacing only a replay of the same round, so bounded repairs remain auditable.
Workflow finalization requires a workflow only for lifecycles with an intermediate state outside initialState and terminalStates; binary inactivation or reversal flags remain valid without one.
A missing workflow suppresses same-entity unreachable and predicate findings. Predicate reachability includes initialState and transition targets.

Lifecycle findings default to shrinkLifecycle in workflow compilation only and are persisted with operateState as an alternative. Fixed-point cascade decisions and evidence-backed workflow omission are passed to the unchanged post-resolution gate; a gate failure after resolution remains a terminal Type A invariant assertion. These findings never trigger an LLM retry or a mandatory human checkpoint.
Full transitions live only in workflow artifacts; use cases and journeys keep transition refs. Global source hashes, language and timestamps live only in indexes.
Journey business blocks and businessHash values are immutable; E7 writes only resolution/realization metadata.
E7 has no routine human checkpoint. E6 remains the sixth and final product-design clarification; recorded lifecycle decisions may be revisited explicitly later without blocking ordinary compilation.

steps.goal: Compile every workspace of the module — record catalogues, journey screens and the anchor hub — from the approved E2-E7 contracts.
runtimeNotes: E8 compiles the whole workspace model in one pass and persists it; there is no worker fan-out, because organisms and command inputs are derived, not written by an LLM.

The approved workspace model is a permanent artifact at the module root, never a pipeline draft: pipeline/ is working state for one run and is discarded afterwards, while E9 and E10 read the model as the contract of record.

The only LLM call composes the hub record page over its closed catalogue. A module with no dominant anchor makes no call at all, and labels are never asked for: every title already arrives localized from an approved E2 or E4 artifact.
An invalid composition receives one constrained repair through the existing presentation-repair plan id; after that the derived order wins with a recorded system decision and the run continues.

Code compiles every workspace of the module from the approved contracts: one record catalogue per persisted business entity, one workspace per approved journey that E2 did not demote, the hub of the dominant anchor and one page per standalone projection. There is no clustering and no invented partition.

A journey workspace emits one query call per locate/inspect step and one command call per act/decide/handoff step, and one section per step in the order of the journey; the locate section renders the picker.

A record catalogue synthesizes its four operations from the ontology, because E7 compiles journeys and a catalogue is not a journey. Its inputs are classified structurally: identity and foreign keys are chosen, a platform-owned parent is the session, a lifecycle status and a timestamp are set by the server, everything else is typed. A state transition never belongs to a catalogue.
An entity no journey operates still gets its catalogue; the audience falls back to the internal profiles and the choice is recorded as a system decision instead of leaving the data unreachable.
The validation report is persisted before any throw, so an irrecoverable model stays auditable.

A broken organism reference is detected exactly as before and resolved deterministically instead of ending the run: a source that names another workspace's query becomes a local call over the same shared operation, an action that names a journey becomes a navigation target of the site map, and a reference that resolves to nothing drops its organism with a recorded decision. Only a model that cannot render at all stays terminal.
A journey is reached from the hub by navigation, carrying the prominence and order the composition chose; it is never an embedded command of the hub page.

steps.goal: Transpose the approved E8 workspace model into the classic L4 format: workspaces, operations, contracts and site map.
input: approved journeys, access, ontology, use cases and compiled workflows
runtimeNotes: beforePromptStep performs the entire compile and returns completed or failed status; E9 never emits prompt_ready and afterPromptStep is an invariant failure path.

The compiler validates context provenance, actor-compatible edges, real carried-context providers, actor journey reachability and queue evidence against compiled E7 workflows. Route membership is derived structurally; shared identifier field names such as projectId are never membership evidence.

Hub collection and record routes, nested place routes, focused scenario routes and standalone routes are derived by the shared total routeOf helper from stable workspace/scenario ids and unique primary use-case targets. Ambiguous targets omit the optional item id and emit a system decision. URL path ids hydrate first; the per-tab store is only a cache.

Handoff and eventDriven delivery is compiled into notifications from the handoff targetProfile and the sending step entity, with a route-backed deep link. Notification delivery is not kept as a navigation edge.

One view contract per workspace plus one command contract per hosted command records exact typed inputs, projected outputs, business errors, source metadata, routePattern, skeletonHash and workspaceHash. Data inputs require ontology field refs, even when their interaction source is userDecision. Verb decisions are identified by policy sourceRef plus absent fieldRef, carry E7 transitionIds as literalUnion metadata and never fabricate a fieldRef. JSON fields and decisions without transitions become unknown with a warning.
Empty organism labels resolve from the approved E4 field title. A missing title records a non-blocking warning without inventing localized text.
Access realization maps every emitted operation route to its exact E3 authority refs through frozen scenario step/use-case ownership.
All emitted arrays and file order are stable, hashes are source hashes only, and no generated timestamp is written, making a no-change rerun byte-identical.

Every gate issue records origin=skeleton or origin=compiler. A skeleton failure marks E8 stale and repairs e8-workspaces; a compiler failure leaves E8 approved and repairs e9-navigation-compiler. Neither failure adds e9-result. A successful compile atomically advances module/pipeline ownership to E10.

steps.goal: Validate the complete approved L4 graph, emit additive L5 delivery contracts and complete the pipeline automatically.
input: approved E2 through E9 permanent L4 artifacts
runtimeNotes: E10 validates the approved workspace model and the classic L4 that E9 wrote. Its authority over E8 and E9 is recompilation: the model is compiled again and compared with the saved artifacts, so a file edited by hand is stale, not a variant.
The named checks keep their contract: A1 model integrity, A2 journey hosting, A3 decision coherence, A4 disclosure registrar, A5 lifecycle health, A6 staleness, A7 warnings and A8 dormant commands.
beforePromptStep performs validate-all and L5 compilation without an LLM. afterPromptStep is an invariant failure path.
Blocking validation persists the report, marks its earliest owning step stale and does not write or update L5 files.

The L5 config merger updates only the current module navigation/headerLinks in an existing client project or top-level module seed. Unrelated keys and modules are preserved; identical inputs produce byte-identical config JSON.
